title: The "Mambo U.S.A." tour with Joe Loco
summary: Conceived by George Gomez to promote Tico records, it gave a good contract and exposure; Puente joined, Tito Rodriguez never did.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: ... okay. Macho in 1954, in the beginning of '55, you and Joe Loco were involved in "Mambo U.S.A." Do you remember anything about that concert tour?
Very, very interesting because Joe Loco was my piano player. I know from one note to another, as soon as he was going to put the finger I know what is going to sound ......
But there were other things.... but, he had his own band at the time.....
... and you had your band and ....
Would you say that "Mambo U.S.A.", which was conceived by George Gomez, to help with your record sales and Tico records sales, Did it help, did it realize?

Oh, yes because you give the opportunity to people to listen in person, then meet you - because you could sell record in China, they never saw you and they might consider; Well, he is a good band, but what about his assets as individual, a showman or whatever, and ......
But what did you get out of that "Mambo U.S.A."?

Well, the contract, it was very good and the experience to be around the United States playing in places that they never saw me, they never saw Joe Loco and the show was fantastic. We had good stars and so we had - everything was right.
Okay, did Tito Rodriguez or Tito Puente ever become part of "Mambo U.S.A."?
Tito Puente yes, Tito Rodriguez, never.
